title: Accounts and Purchasing Administrator
description:
Accounts and Purchasing Administrator

Milton Keynes

Salary: circa £30,000 per annum

Hours 8.30 -5pm

Free Parking

We are recruiting on behalf of a well-established and successful international organisation for an Accounts, Purchasing Administrator to join their busy team in Milton Keynes.

This varied role will support the Accounts, Purchasing and Administration functions, ensuring the smooth running of financial processes while providing administrative support across multiple departments. This is an excellent opportunity for someone who enjoys a hands-on role and thrives in a fast-paced environment where accuracy and attention to detail are essential.

The Role

Reporting to the Accounts, Purchasing and Administration Supervisor, you will be responsible for supporting accounts payable, purchasing activities and general office administration.

Key Responsibilities

Accounts Payable & Finance
- Processing and coding supplier invoices
- Posting vouchers and payment transactions within the ERP system
- Managing Accounts Payable ledgers and reconciliations
- Processing employee expenses through Concur and manual systems
- Creating Accounts Payable payment runs
- Performing vendor statement reconciliations
- Investigating and reconciling freight invoices
- Supporting General Ledger reconciliations
- Producing cash requirement reports
- Maintaining supplier records and vendor spreadsheets
- Recording Postponed VAT Accounting transactions

Purchasing
- Raising and issuing purchase orders
- Monitoring goods receipt and supplier invoices
- Supporting supplier management and maintaining competitive pricing
- Conducting supplier research and price comparisons
- Carrying out regular pricing reviews
- Ensuring purchasing procedures are maintained and updated

Administration
- Reviewing credit applications
- Managing petty cash and month-end reporting
- Providing reception cover, including answering calls and welcoming visitors
- Maintaining filing systems and company records
- Coordinating travel, accommodation and visitor arrangements
- Supporting trade show administration and expenditure tracking
- Monitoring and distributing marketing materials
- Providing general administrative support across departments
- Supporting Accounts Receivable and wider administration teams when required

About You

To be successful in this role, you will have:
- Previous Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable and Purchasing experience ideally
- Strong administration and organisational skills
- Excellent attention to detail and accuracy
- Strong numerical and analytical abilities
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel
- Experience working with ERP or finance systems
- Ability to work with both manual and semi-automated processes
- Excellent communication and relationship-building skills

Personal Attributes
- Self-motivated with a proactive approach
- Strong problem-solving skills and ability to use initiative
- Comfortable working independently and as part of a small team
- Professional, confident and personable manner
- Able to manage multiple priorities and work under pressure
- Highly organised with strong planning skills
- Flexible approach to supporting business needs
- Full driving licence preferred

If you're looking for a varied position that combines accounts, purchasing and administration, and you enjoy working in a collaborative environment where no two days are the same, we'd love to hear from you.

title: Amazon PPC Executive
description:
Amazon PPC Executive

Location: Milton Keynes

Our client is looking for an Amazon PPC Executive to join their team on a full time permeant basis. As an Amazon PPC Executive, you will be at the forefront of managing and optimising Amazon advertising campaigns to drive traffic and sales. This role requires a blend of technical expertise, analytical skills, and strong communication abilities. You will play a pivotal role in the company's marketing efforts, ensuring that advertising campaigns are performing optimally and contributing to the business's success.

Key Duties and Responsibilities:
- Conduct keyword research to identify relevant and high-traffic keywords for ad campaigns.
- Create and launch PPC campaigns on Amazon using tools such as Amazon Advertising Console.
- Write compelling ad copy that accurately represents the product and entices customers to click.
- Monitor and adjust bids to ensure optimal campaign performance while staying within budget.
- Analyse campaign data and make adjustments to improve performance, such as targeting and ad placement.
- Produce reports that clearly communicate campaign results and insights to the team.
- Conduct A/B tests to determine the most effective ad copy, keywords, and targeting strategies.
- Manage advertising budgets to align spending with business goals and objectives.
- Analyse competitor advertising campaigns to identify opportunities and threats.
- Stay up-to-date with industry trends and changes to Amazon's advertising platform.

Skills and Experience:
- Proven expertise in PPC advertising principles and best practices.
- Strong analytical skills to analyse campaign performance data and produce insightful reports.
- Knowledge of keyword research tools and techniques.
- Ability to write compelling and effective ad copy.
- Experience managing bid strategies and budgets for optimal campaign performance.
- Strong communication and collaboration skills to work effectively across various teams.
- Attention to detail to ensure campaigns are set up and managed correctly.
- A willingness to stay current with industry trends and changes.

Company Benefits:
- Casual dress
- On-site parking
- Regular social events including summer and end-of-year parties
- Spontaneous employee well-being treats
- Vouchers at Christmas to shop with the company
- Private medical insurance
- Gym membership discounts

title: Credit Controller - Temp 8 - 12 weeks
description:
Milton Keynes Temp 8 - 12 weeks

Are you an experienced Credit Controller looking for your next opportunity with a company where you can develop your skills and build a long-term career?

We are currently recruiting for a Credit Controller to join a well-established business in Milton Keynes.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone with a background in credit control or accounts receivable who enjoys building customer relationships, resolving queries and taking ownership of their accounts.

The opportunity

£15.38 £17.95 per hour, depending on skills and experience

Temp 8 - 12 weeks

Office-based

Milton Keynes location

Opportunity to develop your credit control and wider finance skill set

Supportive finance team and a business offering long-term career potential

About the role

Working closely with the Financial Controller, you will be responsible for managing an assigned portfolio of accounts and ensuring outstanding debt is effectively controlled and collected.

Your responsibilities will include:

Proactively managing aged debt and reducing outstanding balances.

Contacting customers by telephone, email and letter to negotiate payment of overdue invoices.

Negotiating payment plans and agreeing appropriate repayment arrangements where required.

Reconciling customer accounts to establish accurate debt positions.

Placing accounts on hold when agreed credit limits are exceeded.

Identifying and allocating customer payments accurately and within agreed timescales.

Responding promptly and professionally to customer account queries.

Investigating invoice discrepancies and ensuring required corrections are communicated to the relevant teams

Conducting credit reviews and recommending appropriate credit limits for new and existing customers.

Providing advice to Customer Service and Order Processing teams regarding customers with low credit limits or previous bad debt.

Communicating information regarding bad debtors to relevant clients and representatives and working collaboratively on repayment plans.

Ensuring credit memos are processed accurately and within company guidelines.

Managing cash allocation and lockbox activities.

Reviewing accounts on hold daily and releasing accounts where appropriate.

Setting up new customer accounts and ensuring all information is accurate and complete.

Providing cover for colleagues when required.

Supporting adhoc finance projects and other duties as directed by the Financial Controller.

About you

We are looking for someone who has:
- At least 1 year's experience in Credit Control, Accounts Receivable or a similar finance role.
- Good working knowledge of Microsoft Excel and Word.
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
- Strong attention to detail and accuracy.
- Good problem-solving skills.
- The ability to negotiate confidently and professionally with customers.
- A proactive approach to managing outstanding debt.
- The ability to prioritise effectively and adapt to changing workloads.
- A professional and customer-focused approach.

GCSEs including Maths and English (Grade C/4 or above) are desirable.

Quality Personnel acting as an Employment Agency & Business (rated as one of the top 3 Agencies in Milton Keynes for the 6th year running!).

Please note due to the volume of applications we receive you will only be contacted if we are progressing your application.

company: Bletchley Park Trust Limited - Agency - Permanent
description:
Job Title: HR Coordinator

Location: Bletchley Park Sherwood Drive Bletchley Milton Keynes MK3 6 EB

Salary: £27,500 - £29,000 per annum (depending on experience)

Job type: Permanent, Full Time

Working Hours: 37.5 hours per week

Closing Date: Tuesday 3 November 2026, 12.00 noon.

About us:

Bletchley Park is a vibrant heritage attraction, open daily to visitors, revealing the secrets and telling fascinating stories of the secret British World War Two codebreaking operations. The mission of the Bletchley Park Trust is to attract, engage and educate people from all over the world in order to inspire them with Bletchley Park's crucial role in World War Two.

Bletchley Park is a great place to work. Our people are our biggest resource, and we are committed to value, invest in and nurture our team.

About the role:

We have an exciting opportunity for an HR Coordinator to join our team.

Reporting to the Head of HR, you will provide efficient HR coordination and administrative support throughout the employee and volunteer lifecycles. Key duties include coordinating recruitment and onboarding, completing DBS checks, supporting probationary processes and maintaining accurate HR, volunteer and learning records.

You will provide first line HR support to managers, staff and volunteers in line with our policies and employment legislation. You will also support meetings and take accurate notes while maintaining confidentiality and acting with discretion. As part of a small collaborative team, you will also help deliver team social activities, when required.

About you:

To succeed in this role, you will:
- Be approachable, discreet and organised
- Have strong communication skills and excellent attention to detail.
- Have previous HR administration experience, confidence using HR systems and be proficient in Microsoft Office, including Word, Excel, Teams and SharePoint (essential).
- Support towards a Level 3 HR Support Apprenticeship, or a similar recognised HR qualification may be available, subject to eligibility and funding.

Please click apply to see further details around the person requirements and responsibilities for this role. This is also available to view on the Bletchley Park website.

- Based on site at Bletchley Park, Milton Keynes (MK3 6 EB)
- Salary £27,500 to £29,000 per annum, depending on experience.

Our benefits include:
- 33 days annual leave per year (including statutory holidays).
- Access to our BUPA Cash Plan and Employee Assistance Scheme

- A days' birthday leave (after 12 months service)
- Staff and Volunteer social and wellbeing events

Additional Information:

Closing date for applications: 3 November 2026, 12.00 noon.

Please include a cover letter setting out why you are suitable for this role with your application.

Bletchley Park Trust is committed to, and values the principles of diversity, equality, and inclusion. We strive to provide an inclusive and supportive working environment where all our team feel respected and supported in fulfilling their potential. We acknowledge and value the benefits of a diverse workforce and welcome applications from people of all backgrounds and are committed to ensuring that our recruitment process is transparent, fair and as inclusive as possible for all applicants. We are also committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and adults at risk and expect all staff, volunteers and external agencies to share this commitment.

So that you can fully understand the way we use your data, please refer to our Privacy Policy for Recruitment, which can be found on our website.

No agencies please.

title: Stock Administrator
description:

- Print product and shipping labels.
- Update production schedules and planning information.

- Update warehouse and inventory records.

Essential
- Previous experience working within a manufacturing, production, engineering, assembly, or industrial environment.

- Strong understanding of production processes and inventory accuracy.

title: Youth Mentoring Coordinator
description:
Hours: 37.5 hours per week (full-time)
Contract: 3-year fixed-term contract

Location: Milton Keynes

We're delighted to be partnering with the National Lottery Community Fund as part of our Youth Mentoring MK project. Their funding and support means we're able to expand our mentoring support for children and young people across Milton Keynes, helping those experiencing poverty, disadvantage and discrimination to build confidence, improve their wellbeing and achieve their goals.

We're looking for a passionate, organised and motivated Youth Mentoring Coordinator to help young people build confidence, develop resilience and make positive choices about their future.

You'll play an important role in delivering our community-based mentoring programme, working directly with young people while recruiting, supporting and coordinating a team of volunteer mentors who share our commitment to making a difference.

This is a role for someone who loves working with young people, enjoys bringing people together and wants to create meaningful, lasting impact in their community.

The opportunity

We believe every young person deserves to feel supported, valued and able to reach their potential, whatever challenges they may face.

As our Youth Mentoring Coordinator, you'll help deliver a mentoring programme that provides young people with positive role models, trusted relationships and practical support to navigate life's challenges.

You'll work directly with young people who may be experiencing difficulties with their emotional wellbeing, relationships, education or personal circumstances, helping them recognise their strengths, set achievable goals and move towards a more positive future.

You'll also coordinate our volunteer mentors, ensuring they feel confident, supported and equipped to make a real difference.

From recruiting and welcoming new volunteers to matching them with opportunities, providing ongoing guidance and monitoring the quality of mentoring, you'll help create a positive experience for both mentors and young people.

You'll work closely with community organisations, local partners and the wider YMCA team to ensure young people can access the right support and opportunities.

Above all, you'll help create the trusted relationships and consistent support that can change the direction of a young person's life.

What you'll be doing

You'll play a hands-on role in coordinating and delivering our community-based youth mentoring programme.

Your responsibilities will include:
- Building positive, trusting relationships with young people and providing tailored one-to-one mentoring and support.
- Assessing young people's individual needs and developing person-centred mentoring plans with clear, achievable goals.
- Supporting young people to build confidence, resilience, emotional wellbeing, positive relationships and essential life skills.
- Managing a caseload of young people with medium to high levels of risk or support needs, ensuring appropriate safeguarding and support arrangements are in place.
- Recruiting, coordinating and supporting a team of volunteer mentors, helping them feel confident, motivated and equipped to succeed.
- Providing guidance and ongoing support to volunteers, overseeing mentoring activities, session records and safeguarding practices.
- Coordinating volunteer rotas, placements and activities to ensure effective delivery of mentoring services.
- Building positive relationships with community organisations, referral partners and other local services.
- Connecting young people with additional support and opportunities, including wider YMCA services where appropriate.
- Monitoring mentoring outcomes, maintaining accurate records and demonstrating the positive impact of the programme.
- Working collaboratively with colleagues and partners to develop and improve mentoring services for young people across Milton Keynes.

Just as importantly, you'll create an environment where young people feel heard, volunteers feel valued and everyone understands the difference their contribution makes.

About you

We're looking for someone who genuinely cares about young people and believes in the power of positive relationships to change lives.

You'll have experience working with young people, understand the challenges they may face and be confident providing support that is compassionate, practical and tailored to their individual needs.

You'll also enjoy working with volunteers, helping people feel welcomed, supported and motivated to give their best.

You don't need to have held a formal management position, but you will need to be organised, confident coordinating others and comfortable taking responsibility for the effective delivery of mentoring activities.

You'll be someone who:
- Has experience working directly with young people in youth work, mentoring, education, community services or a similar setting.
- Understands the emotional, social and developmental needs of young people.
- Can build positive, trusting relationships with young people from different backgrounds.
- Has experience coordinating, supervising or supporting volunteers, colleagues or others delivering activities.
- Is organised, reliable and confident managing competing priorities and responsibilities.
- Can assess individual needs, develop support plans and monitor progress.
- Understands safeguarding responsibilities, professional boundaries and the importance of managing risk.
- Communicates effectively with young people, volunteers, colleagues and external partners.
- Is compassionate, resilient and able to respond positively to challenging situations.
- Enjoys developing relationships, bringing people together and helping others succeed.
- Takes ownership, follows things through and looks for ways to improve how services are delivered.
- Brings enthusiasm, initiative and a genuine commitment to helping young people thrive.

Experience supporting young people affected by trauma, instability, youth offending or other complex challenges would be particularly valuable.

Experience recruiting, training or coordinating volunteers within a charity, community or youth organisation would also be an advantage.

A relevant degree-level qualification in youth work, social work, education, social sciences or a related field would be beneficial but isn't essential.

Why Join YMCA South Midlands?

Because this is an opportunity to make a genuine difference, not just to the young people we support, but to the volunteers who give their time to help others.

You'll join an organisation that believes in the potential of every young person and the power of strong communities to create positive change.

As part of our Youth & Community team, you'll have the opportunity to:
- Build meaningful relationships and help young people overcome challenges and achieve their potential.
- Recruit, support and develop a committed team of volunteer mentors.
- Play an important role in delivering and improving our community-based mentoring programme.
- Work with local organisations and partners to create more opportunities for young people.
- Be part of a supportive, collaborative team that genuinely cares about making a difference.
- See the positive impact of your work on young people, volunteers and the wider community.

Everyone is Welcome Here

At YMCA South Midlands, we believe everyone should feel they belong.

We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, experiences and communities. We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive workforce that reflects the people we serve and where everyone is treated with dignity, respect and fairness.

As a charity with a Christian heritage, our faith inspires our values and our commitment to serving others. We welcome people of all faiths and none. All appointments are made on merit.

Safeguarding

YMCA South Midlands is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people. The successful candidate will be required to complete appropriate safer recruitment checks, including an enhanced DBS check and a children's barred list check where the role is eligible.

Reasonable Adjustments

We want every candidate to have the opportunity to perform at their best throughout our recruitment process.

If you have a disability, long-term health condition or are neurodivergent and would benefit from any reasonable adjustments during the recruitment process, please let us know when you apply or contact us at any stage. We'll be happy to discuss how we can support you.

A note to recruitment agencies: We are managing recruitment for this role directly and are not seeking support from recruitment agencies. Please do not submit speculative CVs or contact us regarding this vacancy.

title: Receptionist
description: We are looking for a Receptionist/Administrator to join our friendly and supportive team at Purbeck Health Centre. This is an important front-line role where you will help patients access the right care while supporting the smooth day-to-day running of the practice. Friendly, approachable and professional Reliable, organised and able to manage competing priorities Confident communicating with patients and colleagues Comfortable using computers and learning new systems Able to work independently and as part of a team Committed to providing excellent patient service Previous experience in a GP practice or healthcare setting would be helpful, but it is not essential. Full training will be provided, and you will be supported by an experienced team who take pride in delivering excellent care and service to our patients. If you are looking for a rewarding and varied role where you can make a real difference to patients every day, we would love to hear from you. What you will be doing Answering telephone calls and responding to patient enquiries Welcoming patients at the reception desk Booking and managing appointments Completing a variety of administrative tasks Working closely with our clinical and administrative teams Handling confidential information professionally The role is busy and varied, so you will need excellent communication and organisational skills, good attention to detail, and the ability to remain calm under pressure. Job Description Job title: Receptionist/Administrator Location: Purbeck Health Centre, Milton Keynes Hours: Working pattern to be agreed Reports to: Reception Lead/Practice Manager The Receptionist/Administrator will be one of the first points of contact for patients and visitors. The postholder will provide a professional and welcoming reception service, manage telephone calls and patient enquiries, and complete a range of computer-based administrative duties. The role is essential to supporting the smooth day-to-day running of the practice and ensuring patients receive a helpful, efficient and respectful service. Welcome patients and visitors in a friendly, caring and professional manner. Check patients in for appointments and assist with general enquiries. Support the smooth flow of patients through the practice. Communicate with clinicians and other team members when required. Keep the reception area calm, tidy and organised. Respect patients privacy and maintain confidentiality at all times. Answer incoming telephone calls promptly and courteously. Book, amend and cancel appointments accurately using SystmOne. Respond to general enquiries and direct patients to the appropriate service or member of staff. Follow practice procedures when receiving urgent or emergency calls and escalate concerns immediately where required. Take clear and accurate messages and pass them to the appropriate clinician or administrator promptly. Communicate sensitively with patients who may be worried, distressed or frustrated. Update patient contact details, appointment information and records accurately. Process online appointment requests, messages and administrative queries. Maintain accurate patient records, tasks and worklists on SystmOne. Monitor emails, call queues and other practice communication systems. Support the smooth running of the days appointments and reception services. Complete general administrative duties, including printing letters, preparing lists and entering data. Follow practice procedures for filing, communication and information sharing. Work closely with reception colleagues to maintain appropriate cover for the front desk and telephone lines. Communicate clearly and professionally with clinicians, administrators and management. Provide additional cover during colleagues annual leave or sickness where required. Attend team meetings, training sessions and practice updates. Contribute ideas that could improve patient services or working processes. Promote a positive, respectful and supportive working environment. Follow all practice policies and procedures, including those relating to confidentiality, safeguarding, information governance and data protection. Maintain a professional, respectful and positive approach. Report incidents, risks or concerns promptly to the Reception Lead or Practice Manager. Complete all required mandatory training. Keep knowledge of practice systems, policies and procedures up to date. Work within the responsibilities and boundaries of the role. Excellent communication and telephone skills. A friendly, polite and approachable manner. Confidence using computers and learning new systems. Good organisational skills and the ability to manage competing priorities. Ability to remain calm and professional in a busy environment. Strong attention to detail and accuracy. A reliable, flexible and supportive approach to teamwork. Understanding of the importance of patient confidentiality. Commitment to providing a high standard of patient service. Previous experience in a GP practice, healthcare setting or customer-facing role. Experience using SystmOne or another clinical record system. The postholder must promote equality, diversity and inclusion and treat all patients, visitors and colleagues with dignity, fairness and respect. The postholder must take reasonable care of their own health and safety and that of others who may be affected by their work. Any hazards, incidents or concerns must be reported promptly in accordance with practice procedures. All patient, staff and practice information must be treated as confidential. The postholder must follow UK GDPR, data protection requirements, NHS information governance standards and practice policies. The postholder will be expected to: Uphold the values and reputation of Purbeck Health Centre. Follow all practice policies, procedures and applicable NHS requirements. Take responsibility for their own learning, training and professional development. Contribute to a positive, supportive and inclusive workplace. Carry out other reasonable duties appropriate to the role. This job description provides an overview of the role and is not exhaustive. Duties may change as the needs of the practice develop, following appropriate discussion with the postholder and their line manager.

title: Medical Receptionist
description: Ashfield Medical Centre is a very busy and friendly GP Practice in Milton Keynes. We are currently looking to add to our fabulous reception team with a morning receptionist. Hours to be worked at 7am till 1pm Monday to Friday (with the possibility of overtime covering the afternoon shift of 1pm till 7pm as required). We would prefer that you have experience of working within a GP Practice environment or previous NHS experience and working knowledge of Systm1 but full training can be provided in any case for the right candidate. The job is demanding but rewarding so great teamwork and a good sense of humour will be essential! Starting salary £13.00 per hour rising to £13.25 per hour after successful completion of the probationary period and training. Key skills required for the role included face to face engagement with the public, excellent telephone manner, clear and precise typing and writing, ability to work on own or as part of a team, knowledge of medical terminology and ability to raise prescriptions ready for electronic signing. Out reception team also work as chaperones when required for the GPs and Nursing Team. All necessary training will be provided. This list is not exhaustive. Job summary: The purpose of the role is to: Offer general assistance to the practice team and project a positive and friendly image to patients and other visitors, either in person or via the telephone Receive, assist and direct patients in accessing the appropriate service or healthcare professional in a courteous, efficient and effective way Undertake a variety of administrative duties to assist in the smooth running of the practice including the provision of secretarial and clerical support to clinical staff and other members of the practice team Facilitate effective communication between patients, members the primary health care team, secondary care and other associated healthcare agencies Duties and responsibilities: The duties and responsibilities to be undertaken by members of the practice administration team may include any or all of the items in the following list. Duties may be varied from time to time under the direction of the senior receptionist/practice manager, dependent on current and evolving practice workload and staffing levels: Opening up/locking-up of practice premises and maintaining security in accordance with Practice protocols Maintaining and monitoring the practice appointments system Processing personal and telephone requests for appointments, visits and telephone consultations and ensuring callers are directed to the appropriate healthcare professional Processing and distributing incoming (and outgoing) mail Taking messages and passing on information Filing and retrieving paperwork Processing repeat prescriptions in accordance with practice guidelines Computer data entry/data allocation and collation; processing and recording information in accordance with practice procedures Initiating contact with and responding to requests from patients, other team member and associated healthcare agencies and providers Clearing and re-stock consulting rooms as required Providing clerical assistance to practice staff as required from time to time, including word/data processing, filing, photocopying and scanning Provision of refreshments for staff and visitors as required; loading and emptying the dishwasher and keeping the kitchen area clean and tidy Keeping the reception area, notice-boards and leaflet dispensers tidy and free from obstructions and clutter Any other delegated duties appropriate to the post Confidentiality: In the course of seeking treatment, patients entrust us with, or allow us to gather, sensitive information in relation to their health and other matters. They do so in confidence and have the right to expect that staff will respect their privacy and act appropriately In the performance of the duties outlined in this job description, the post-holder may have access to confidential information relating to patients and their carers, practice staff and other healthcare workers. They may also have access to information relating to the practice as a business organisation. All such information from any source is to be regarded as strictly confidential Information relating to patients, carers, colleagues, other healthcare workers or the business of the practice may only be divulged to authorised persons in accordance with the practice policies and procedures relating to confidentiality and the protection of personal and sensitive data Health & Safety: The post-holder will assist in promoting and maintaining their own and others health, safety and security as defined in the practice health & safety policy, the practice health & safety manual, and the practice infection control policy and published procedures. This will include: Using personal security systems within the workplace according to practice guidelines Identifying the risks involved in work activities and undertaking such activities in a way that manages those risks Making effective use of training to update knowledge and skills Using appropriate infection control procedures, maintaining work areas in a tidy and safe way and free from hazards Actively reporting of health and safety hazards and infection hazards immediately when recognised Keeping own work areas and general / patient areas generally clean, assisting in the maintenance of general standards of cleanliness consistent with the scope of the job holders role Undertaking periodic infection control training (minimum annually) Reporting potential risks identified Equality and diversity: The post-holder will support the equality, diversity and rights of patients, carers and colleagues, to include: Acting in a way that recognises the importance of peoples rights, interpreting them in a way that is consistent with practice procedures and policies, and current legislation Respecting the privacy, dignity, needs and beliefs of patients, carers and colleagues Behaving in a manner which is welcoming to and of the individual, is non-judgmental and respects their circumstances, feelings priorities and rights. Personal/professional development: The post-holder will participate in any training programme implemented by the practice as part of this employment, such training to include: Participation in an annual individual performance review, including taking responsibility for maintaining a record of own personal and/or professional development Taking responsibility for own development, learning and performance and demonstrating skills and activities to others who are undertaking similar work Quality: The post-holder will strive to maintain quality within the practice, and will: Alert other team members to issues of quality and risk Assess own performance and take accountability for own actions, either directly or under supervision Contribute to the effectiveness of the team by reflecting on own and team activities and making suggestions on ways to improve and enhance the teams performance Work effectively with individuals in other agencies to meet patients needs Effectively manage own time, workload and resources Communication: The post-holder should recognize the importance of effective communication within the team and will strive to: Communicate effectively with other team members Communicate effectively with patients and carers Recognize peoples needs for alternative methods of communication and respond accordingly Contribution to the implementation of services: The post-holder will: Apply practice policies, standards and guidance
